sugestoes.texto: The `message` variable in the catch block is now unused. This is dead code rather than a comment or string mismatch, so remove it or use it.

issues.descricao: Claims GoogleCalendarService.createEvent/updateEvent dereference an undefined mainHostDestinationCalendar when destinationCalendar is null or empty.
destinationCalendar is defaulted to null in some producers and to an empty array in others.
loadUsers no longer selects organization.slug for dynamic-user bookings, so code reading user.organization gets undefined.

Claims that for references without a credentialId, looping over every calendar reference and deleting each against all user calendar credentials produces duplicate or wrong-target delete calls and errors.

sugestoes.texto: The error toast renders the raw server `err.message` (and error code) directly. Unexpected backend failures such as Prisma errors from the handler can carry internal details that end up displayed to the user. Only show the message when it is a known translation key, otherwise fall back to the generic `unable_to_add_guests` text.

issues.descricao: Claims newGuests.includes(attendee.email) misroutes newly added guests whose casing differs from the stored value, but new attendees are stored with exactly the submitted string.
Suggests starting with [] instead of [""] because the empty string may cause validation issues; the empty initial field is intentional and validated.
sendAddGuestsEmails never notifies the newly added guests because the formatted event does not contain them, so the newGuests branch is unreachable.
OrganizerAddGuestsEmail reads calEvent.attendees[0].name without a guard and throws when the attendee list is empty.

sugestoes.texto: The decryption key falls back to an empty string when CALCOM_APP_CREDENTIAL_ENCRYPTION_KEY is unset. A critical key should not have a weak default. Fail fast with an explicit error if the key is missing.

issues.descricao: Claims the JSDoc describes appData.type as 'the app slug', copied from appData.appId.
Claims the team-credential branch only checks accepted membership instead of admin rights, letting non-admin members create team credentials.
Claims malformed OAuth state makes JSON.parse throw and crash OAuth callbacks with a 500.
Claims the Office365 video adapter passes the wrong app slug 'msteams' to refreshOAuthTokens.
createOAuthAppCredential only verifies team membership, not admin access, before creating a team credential, so any team member can install OAuth apps for the team via a crafted state.

sugestoes.texto: `expect(locator.isChecked()).toBeTruthy()` asserts on an un-awaited Promise, so it always passes. The enable flow now ends on the backup-codes dialog, which this test never closes, so the test cannot detect a failure to enable 2FA. Close the dialog via `backup-codes-close` and assert `[data-testid=two-factor-switch][data-state="checked"]` is visible, as the second test does.

issues.descricao: Claims a caller of the changed TwoFactorAuthAPI.disable still passes two arguments, but that caller uses a different, unchanged API module.
The enable-2FA test asserts toBeTruthy on the un-awaited isChecked() Promise, so it passes regardless of the switch state, including now that the backup-codes step is never dismissed.
Backup codes are compared with indexOf/=== instead of a constant-time comparison, theoretically leaking timing information.
Suggests a clearer post-2FA redirect journey in a file that does not exist.
Claims a 2FA page leaks a polling interval; no such page or interval exists.
Reports no issue.
The first 2FA e2e test asserts toBeTruthy() on an unawaited isChecked() Promise, so it always passes even though the backup-codes step now keeps 2FA unchecked until Close is clicked.

sugestoes.texto: WHAT: The template closes the conditional with `<%- end if %>`, which is a trailing `if` modifier on `end`. WHY: it is a syntax hazard, because the following template output becomes the modifier's condition. The header branches may then render incorrectly or the template may raise a SyntaxError. HOW: use `<%- end %>`.

The controller enqueues Jobs :retrieve_topic when no embed exists, but spec/controllers/embed_controller_spec.rb expects TopicRetriever.new(...).retrieve to be called from the controller. The spec and the implementation disagree, so the 'tells the topic retriever to work' example fails. Either call the retriever or change the spec to expect the job to be enqueued.

request.referer is written into a JavaScript string literal with HTML escaping (`<%= %>`), which is not JS escaping. Characters such as `&` turn into HTML entities, and backslashes or newlines are not JS-escaped. Emit the value with `.to_json` or `escape_javascript` instead.

issues.descricao: Claims embed.js throws a TypeError when the page lacks the #discourse-comments element because comments.appendChild is called on null.
Claims the embed controller spec fails because EmbedController#best only enqueues a Sidekiq job and never constructs TopicRetriever during the request.
The hourly PollFeed job always fetches and processes the full feed without a conditional GET; the feed_key helper meant for that is defined but never used.
States that the link fallback in PollFeed is correct; no problem is reported.
States the raw_html cook_method comparison in Post#cook is safe; no problem is reported.
States the cook_method assignment in PostCreator is correct; no problem is reported.
States the `if topic_id` check in EmbedController is safe; no problem is reported.
Describes the host checks in ensure_embeddable without reporting a problem.
States content_sha1 and absolutize_urls in TopicEmbed are correct; no problem is reported.
States the TopicRetriever throttle uses setnx and an explicit no_throttle check; no problem is reported.
Claims import_remote passes an unvalidated user-supplied URL to Kernel#open, allowing command execution with '|' or local file reads.
Claims PollFeed fetches SiteSetting.feed_polling_url without validation, letting whoever controls that setting make the server request arbitrary internal or external URLs.
Claims the embed best.html.erb template closes its if block with `end if`, which is invalid Ruby, so every render raises a SyntaxError.
The embed layout interpolates request.referer into an inline JavaScript string with only HTML escaping, so a referer containing a quote can break out of the string and run script.
Claims postMessage drops the resize message because targetOrigin is the full referer URL rather than just the origin, breaking iframe auto-resize.
Claims setting X-Frame-Options: ALLOWALL on the embed endpoint disables clickjacking protection and that the referer check can be spoofed.
Claims the cook_method migration default of 1 equals raw_html, so every post would skip cooking and sanitization.
Claims the 'not a url' TopicRetriever spec passes regardless of the InvalidURIError rescue because embeddable_host is blank.
`<%- end if %>` in embed/best.html.erb is not valid Ruby, so the template raises a SyntaxError and the embed page fails to render.
Claims `<%- end if %>` leaves a dangling if modifier that makes the logo output the condition, so the logo renders before the header button.
Claims the embed best action builds the view for current_user and then marks it publicly cacheable, so a staff member's view could be served to anonymous visitors.

sugestoes.texto: `group.users.delete(user_id)` with a raw integer id looks the record up through the association and raises ActiveRecord::RecordNotFound if the user is not (or is no longer) a member. This happens when two admins remove the same member, or on a stale member list, and it returns a 500/404 instead of succeeding silently. Look the user up first and delete it only if it is present in the group.

issues.descricao: Claims the now-unawaited findMembers() call creates a race where the controller has no member data available when it needs it.
Claims the public group members template iterates a bare members property that resolves to undefined because the controller's model is now the Group object.
Claims add_members/remove_member read params[:group_id] while the route supplies the group id as params[:id], so the actions always fail with ParameterMissing.
Claims add_members does not strip whitespace around comma-separated usernames, so entries like 'alice, bob' silently fail to add members.
Claims the public members endpoint accepts an unbounded or negative limit/offset, letting a caller force loading and serializing the whole membership of a large group.

sugestoes.texto: ProvideAnonDBStore now requires a `deviceLimit int64` argument, but pkg/server/wire.go:374-375 still lists it as a wire provider and binds AnonStore to *AnonDBStore. Wire cannot satisfy a bare int64 parameter, so wire generation or the build breaks. impl.go no longer consumes an injected AnonStore, so remove the provider and the bind from wire.go and regenerate wire_gen.go.

issues.descricao: Claims ProvideAnonDBStore's new int64 parameter breaks wire dependency injection because wire.go still registers it.
Claims updateDevice reports ErrDeviceLimitReached for any zero-row update, conflating missing or stale devices with the limit being reached.
Claims anonymous clients can bypass the device limit by omitting the X-Grafana-Device-Id header.
Claims anonymous authentication now fails entirely when TagDevice returns ErrDeviceLimitReached, instead of the previous non-blocking async tagging.
Claims TagDevice now propagates all tagging errors instead of only the limit error, breaking callers that ignored them.
Claims updateDevice's time window is based on device.UpdatedAt rather than time.Now(), which may not match the intended logic.
ProvideAnonDBStore gained an int64 deviceLimit parameter but is still registered as a wire provider in pkg/server/wire.go, which has no provider for int64, so wire generation or compilation fails.

ProvideAnonDBStore now takes an int64 deviceLimit but is still registered as a Wire provider (with an AnonStore bind) in pkg/server/wire.go; Wire cannot supply an int64, so DI generation and the server build fail.
Claims updateDevice's RowsAffected()==0 check wrongly denies already-registered devices on MySQL because MySQL reports changed rather than matched rows.
CreateOrUpdateDevice runs a full COUNT over the 30-day anon_device table on every anonymous request when a device limit is set.

sugestoes.texto: The old LoggerMiddleware attached traceID to the 'Plugin Request Completed' log, and the new contextual-logger middleware that replaced that enrichment does not re-add it. logRequest now uses only FromContext(ctx), and ConcreteLogger.FromContext does not add traceID, so the log line loses trace correlation. Add traceID from tracing.TraceIDFromContext(ctx, false) to the attributes in instrumentContext.

issues.descricao: Claims ContextualLoggerMiddleware panics on nil requests because it reads req.PluginContext without a nil guard.
Claims the refactor dropped traceID from the 'Plugin Request Completed' log lines.
Claims the metrics middleware factory mutates a shared instance's next field, causing a data race between chains.
Claims the request-size histogram's HELP text says 'returned' though it measures request sizes.
Claims the test never asserts that request size is not instrumented for CheckHealth/CollectMetrics.
Claims checkHistogram carries foundLabels across metrics and returns errors prematurely.
Claims millisecond durations are truncated by integer division before conversion to float.
Claims the request-size test cases use empty payloads and would not detect a broken size calculation.
Claims the duration metric checks only labels and sample counts, not the observed values.
Claims the duration-seconds histogram check omits status and source labels.
Claims LoggerMiddleware depends on ContextualLoggerMiddleware running first and would log without plugin identity if reordered.
Claims the metrics middleware now fails the request when the plugin is not in the registry.
The metrics middleware test never asserts that request size is not recorded for CheckHealth and CollectMetrics.

sugestoes.texto: NewResourceServer now runs s.Init(ctx) synchronously. Construction used to be cheap and never failed on init, and now it blocks on lifecycle hooks, a full search index build and DB stats queries. Any init error, such as DB not ready or migrations not run, now makes the constructor return nil, and callers that built the server first and initialised it later cannot do that any more. Keep the lazy Init, or have callers call Init explicitly at startup, instead of failing construction.

issues.descricao: Claims the new postgres t.Skip removes coverage of the storage-server instrumentation test for that backend.
Claims making NewResourceServer call Init changes the constructor contract, blocking on the full index build and failing construction on any index error.
Claims starting the watcher after search.init makes writes between the index snapshot and initWatcher never reach the search index.
NewResourceServer now runs Init synchronously and fails construction on init error, blocking on index build and watcher startup and changing the constructor contract for callers.

NewResourceServer now runs Init synchronously (lifecycle, full search index build, watcher) and returns an error on failure, so callers that were not changed block on startup and abort construction on Init failure.
Claims write events arriving between search watcher start and initWatcher are consumed by the search reader and never reach Watch subscribers.

sugestoes.texto: WHAT: The NPE fix is applied only to getSubGroupsCount, so the three getSubGroupsStream overloads still call modelSupplier.get().getSubGroupsStream(...) without a null check. WHY: modelSupplier.get() returns null when the group is deleted concurrently, so those paths still throw NullPointerException. HOW: Guard them the same way, for example by returning Stream.empty() when the delegate is null.

There is no positive test showing that allowed HTML (br/p/strong/b) passes verification without errors. The reviewer calls this a coverage gap and not a defect of the 'test passes even if behaviour is broken' class. Consider adding a test where the English and translated values contain only allowed tags and asserting that no errors are reported.

issues.descricao: Claims santizeAnchors consumes English matcher groups without validation, so a translation with more anchor tags than the English text gets incorrect results.
Notes that normalizeValue blanks the whole choice expression, so a wrong argument index inside the choice would not be flagged.
Claims the English-file path rewrite is fragile and that a messages file without an English counterpart aborts the build with a RuntimeException.
Notes no test covers allowed tags under POLICY_SOME_HTML, so emptying the allow-list would not fail the suite.
VerifyMessageProperties loads message bundles with PropertyResourceBundle(InputStream), claimed to decode as ISO-8859-1 and produce mojibake and spurious Illegal HTML failures for non-English files.

sugestoes.texto: WHAT: The listener is gated on ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ (V1), but management() returns MgmtPermissionsV2 whenever V2 is enabled, and this PR makes its clients() return ClientPermissionsV2. ClientPermissionsV2.setPermissionsEnabled throws UnsupportedOperationException. WHY: with V1 and V2 both enabled, removing a client runs management(...).clients().setPermissionsEnabled(client, false), which throws and aborts the client-removal event. HOW: skip the V1 cleanup branches when ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ_V2 is enabled, for example by checking `!Profile.isFeatureEnabled(ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ_V2)` in the ClientRemovedEvent branch, or by giving V2 a non-throwing no-op or cleanup implementation.

testMapRolesAndCompositesOnlyOneClient grants MAP_ROLES, MAP_ROLES_COMPOSITE and CONFIGURE in a single permission, then asserts only that both operations succeed. If canMapRoles or canMapCompositeRoles evaluated the wrong scope, the test would still pass through the user-level MAP_ROLES permission or CONFIGURE. Grant each scope in a separate permission, and assert that the operation is forbidden when only the other scope is present.

issues.descricao: Claims the per-client resource lookup uses server.getId() as owner while resources are created with server.getClientId(), so client-specific permissions are never found.
Claims that with both fine-grained features enabled, client deletion calls ClientPermissionsV2.setPermissionsEnabled and throws UnsupportedOperationException.
Claims the all-clients resource lookup in hasPermission(String) cannot find the resource (owner mismatch or not lazily created), so global client permissions are ignored.
Claims the client management-permissions endpoint returns a 500 under V2 because it calls ClientPermissionsV2 methods that throw UnsupportedOperationException.
Claims hasPermission(client, scope) accepts permissions granted on other resources because it does not filter by resource id, allowing privilege escalation across clients.
Claims getClientsWithPermission runs a separate policy evaluation for every client resource, causing O(N) slowdowns.
ClientPermissionsV2.getClientsWithPermission runs a full policy evaluation for every client resource of type Clients, so listing clients costs one evaluation per client resource.

On ClientRemovedEvent the AdminPermissions listener calls clients().setPermissionsEnabled(client, false), which throws UnsupportedOperationException in ClientPermissionsV2 when V1 and V2 are both enabled, so client deletion fails.
Claims that with both fine-grained authz V1 and V2 enabled, the ClientRemovedEvent listener calls ClientPermissionsV2.setPermissionsEnabled, which now throws, so client deletion fails.
Claims the test grants CONFIGURE together with MAP_ROLES_COMPOSITE, so addComposites may succeed because of CONFIGURE and the test would pass even if canMapCompositeRoles were broken.
Claims that under FGAP V2 the client management-permissions GET/PUT endpoints call the throwing ClientPermissionsV2 overrides and return 500.

sugestoes.texto: AbstractUsernameFormAuthenticator.badPasswordHandler calls challenge(...) while the attempted user is still set in the context, before clearUser(). This override now gates passkey rendering on that user's credentials. After a failed password the page shows passkey elements only if the submitted username has a passkey, which reveals the account's existence and credential type. Only apply the per-user check when the user was set before this authenticator ran (the USER_SET_BEFORE_USERNAME_PASSWORD_AUTH note is true). Otherwise decide on passkeysEnabled alone.

issues.descricao: Claims PasswordForm.authenticate can fill passkey context data for a null user because isConditionalPasskeysEnabled returns true when no user is set, producing an inconsistent password page.
Claims configuredFor marks PasswordForm as configured for passkey-only users, so they land on a password form they cannot satisfy.
Claims action() processes a passkey assertion for a different userHandle during re-authentication, letting another user's passkey satisfy re-auth of the fixed user.
Claims the password page leaks the typed user's passkey credential IDs to an unauthenticated visitor, disclosing whether the account has passkeys.
Claims a Kotlin state manager should use ViewModel + StateFlow for UI state.
Claims UsernameForm.authenticate calls isConditionalPasskeysEnabled() without the required UserModel argument.
Claims isConditionalPasskeysEnabled requires a non-null user, so the initial login page no longer sets up conditional passkey UI for ID-less login.
Reports that widening USER_SET_BEFORE_USERNAME_PASSWORD_AUTH and the reauth form helper expose no sensitive data.
Reports that setupReauthenticationInUsernamePasswordFormError only toggles UI flags and leaks nothing.
Reports that the passkey conditional-UI data is non-secret; no exposure.
Reports that the added error-path calls leak no credential information.
Reports that emitting WebAuthn credential IDs in passkeys.ftl is not sensitive.
Reports that the auth note writer and reader use the same key; refactor is behaviour-preserving.
Reports that the helper reads the same auth note key.
Reports that the constant's value is unchanged by the visibility change.
Reports that isConditionalPasskeysEnabled is reused consistently.
Reports no issue at UsernamePasswordForm.authenticate.
Reports no issue at UsernamePasswordForm.challenge.
Reports no issue at PasswordForm.authenticate.
Reports no issue at PasswordForm.configuredFor.
Reports no unreachable branch in action().
Reports no NPE in PasswordForm.authenticate because the helper checks webauthnAuth != null.
Reports no computed-then-ignored values.
States the authn_use_chk field name could not be checked against the JavaScript; no problem asserted.

The password page now renders an identified user's passkey credential IDs as hidden inputs in the username-first flow before authentication, disclosing credential metadata to anyone who knows a username.

After a username-only step, PasswordForm fills WebAuthn context for the user and passkeys.ftl renders their credential IDs as hidden inputs, letting an unauthenticated visitor learn whether an account has a passkey and its credential IDs.
No test exercises a passkey failure during re-authentication, so the new setupReauthenticationInUsernamePasswordFormError call in WebAuthnConditionalUIAuthenticator is never covered.

sugestoes.texto: The invalidation hooks use LoginFilter.getLoginPredicate(), which now excludes org-linked IDPs that are not BROKER_PUBLIC. getForLogin(mode, organizationId) caches per-org results that may include those IDPs, so changes to them never invalidate the cache and it goes stale. Use an invalidation check that matches what getForLogin actually returns, for example by ignoring the public/org clause for IDPs linked to an organization.

issues.descricao: Claims getForLogin re-enters the caching layer by calling session.identityProviders().getById instead of idpDelegate.getById; this deliberately resolves IDs through the per-IDP cache.
Claims the cache-hit path of getForLogin returns raw, non-organization-aware models; getById already wraps them.
Claims linking/unlinking an IDP to an organization never invalidates the getForLogin caches; the org provider routes through IdentityProviderStorageProvider.update which does.
Claims resolving cached IDs one by one with getById turns login listing into N lookups; those lookups hit the per-IDP cache by design.
Claims the HashSet in cached getForLogin returns IDPs in nondeterministic order; every caller sorts the result.
Claims remove() of a nonexistent alias now dereferences null; the new login invalidation is null-safe and the other call is unchanged pre-existing code.
Claims getLoginPredicate can NPE on a null config; config is always initialized.
Claims org-specific ALL/ORG_ONLY login queries include non-public org IDPs, so the BROKER_PUBLIC gate misses invalidations; the query always requires BROKER_PUBLIC=true.

getForLogin caches all organizations under one realm/mode entry, so each new organizationId invalidates and rebuilds that entry with every previously cached search merged in, instead of caching per organization.

sugestoes.texto: The docstrings say validate_timestamp checks that 'age is absent, but timestamp is present' and validate_age checks that 'age is present, but not timestamp'. The code only rejects the case where both fields are supplied. Both fields are required=False, so a report with neither passes. Reword the docstrings to say they only enforce mutual exclusion, or add a check that one of the two is present.

issues.descricao: Claims the unauthenticated endpoint iterates an unbounded array of reports, allowing CPU/metric-spam DoS.
Claims BrowserReportingCollectorEndpoint returns Django HttpResponse objects although its Endpoint base expects DRF Response objects.
The assemble analytics event is recorded before the feature-flag check, so requests rejected with 404 are still counted as assemble events, skewing analytics.
BaseDetectorTypeValidator.update() reads validated_data.get('detector_type') instead of 'type', so detector type changes are silently ignored.
Claims get_condition_query_groups indexes dcg_to_slow_conditions[dcg.id] and may KeyError for a DCG missing from the precomputed map.
Claims the triggered_actions log now writes the full event payload with user data because event_data was switched to workflow_event_data.
Claims the success path dereferences data.summary without guarding undefined data when the query is disabled or errored.
Claims the column fallback crashes when tableData is defined but meta is missing.
Claims ExploreParams still reads visualize.yAxes after the Visualize class switched to yAxis, producing undefined saved-query params.
Asks to verify that no caller passes Visualize instances instead of BaseVisualize to updateLocationWithAggregateFields.
Claims the number-type test's mock matches query.query instead of substringMatch, so its not-called assertion can never fail.
Claims the attribute key is interpolated into the request path without encodeURIComponent, enabling path confusion.
get_environment_info fetches the recommended event per issue while building the merged-PR comment, an N+1 lookup on the comment path.
The number-type test mock matches on query.query while the hook sends substringMatch, so the mock can never match and the not-called assertion cannot fail.
Claims _truncate_title is defined on CommitContextIntegration, so PRCommentWorkflow._truncate_title raises AttributeError.
Claims the hook now returns undefined attributes before the first fetch instead of {}, which can crash consumers that access keys on the TagCollection.
Claims the default of sentry:autofix_automation_tuning changed from low to off, silently disabling automatic autofix for projects that never set it, unrelated to the replays bulk delete feature.

sugestoes.texto: test_to_dict asserts `queued is not None`, which is always true because `queued` has a default value. The assertion is weak and cannot fail. Assert a concrete expected value for `queued` instead.

issues.descricao: Claims to_dict() returns a raw datetime for queued that fails JSON serialization when passed as Celery task kwargs.
The assignment_source parameter was added to the abstract sync_status_outbound instead of sync_assignee_outbound, which is the method that actually receives it.
Claims concrete integrations overriding should_sync(self, attribute) will raise TypeError at the new two-argument call in sync_assignee_outbound.
Claims a malformed assignment_source_dict makes from_dict return None, so should_sync fails open and re-enables the sync cycle.
test_to_dict asserts queued is not None, which is always true because queued has a default, so the assertion verifies nothing.
Claims passing AssignmentSource.to_dict() with a raw datetime to sync_assignee_outbound.apply_async fails Sentry's bad-pickle check in tests and would break under a JSON serializer.

sync_status_outbound gains an assignment_source parameter that is never threaded through the status task or checked in should_sync, so status sync gets no cycle prevention despite the signature suggesting it.

sugestoes.texto: The OAuth `state` is compared to `pipeline.signature` with `!=`, which is not constant-time. Use `django.utils.crypto.constant_time_compare` for this security token check.

test_github_user_mismatch asserts only the generic "Invalid installation request." message and a failure payload. The state-mismatch, token-exchange, missing-login and integration-not-found paths return the same output, so the test passes even if the sender-versus-authenticated-user comparison is removed. Assert something specific to the mismatch branch. For example, prove the state and OAuth steps succeeded, or give the error a distinct message for this case.

issues.descricao: Claims the OAuth state is compared to the secret pipeline signature in non-constant time, leaking timing information.
Claims other consumers driving GitHubInstallation without the new OAuth view will always be rejected; no such consumer exists.
Claims a null reference when the github_authenticated_user state is missing; the code only compares it and returns the error page.
test_github_user_mismatch asserts only the generic 'Invalid installation request.' message, which any error path would produce.
The GitHub OAuth state parameter is compared with != instead of a constant-time comparison, leaking timing information.
The installation sender-login mismatch test asserts only the generic error text, which state mismatch and OAuth failures also produce, so it cannot show the login check caused the rejection.
The OAuth state check in GitHub OAuthLoginView compares the callback state to pipeline.signature with a plain `!=` instead of a constant-time comparison.
Claims the GitHub OAuth token exchange omits redirect_uri, so GitHub returns redirect_uri_mismatch and every installation fails.
Claims a literal 'null' installation_id passes the None check and routes users to the 'Invalid installation request.' page instead of the app installer.

sugestoes.texto: The comment says "within the threshold of commits", but the code inspects check-ins, not commits. It is misleading prose in this newly added file. Replace "commits" with "check-ins".
The `logger` objects are defined but never used. Remove them, or use them where logging is intended.

issues.descricao: Claims previous_checkins[0] can raise IndexError when the threshold query returns no rows.
Asks to confirm no consumer still imports SimpleCheckIn from mark_failed after it moved to monitors/types.py.
Claims fetching MonitorCheckIn objects by id is an unnecessary query because previous_checkins already has the data.

sugestoes.texto: getSlots now depends on `override.timeZone`, but the shared TimeRange type declares it optional and only getSchedule was updated to populate it. Any other dateOverrides caller that omits timeZone gets `.tz(undefined)`, which does not fall back to the organizer's zone, so the offset is computed wrongly and override slots shift. Make the dependency explicit (a required field on the override type, or a defined fallback such as organizerTimeZone) and update the remaining callers.

The new +6:00 date-override test expects the same UTC slots as the +5:30 case. The pre-change code, which used UTC hours and ignored the invitee timezone, also returns those slots, so the test would pass if the offset logic in slots.ts were reverted. Use a timezone and override combination where the old and new logic produce different slots, and assert the offset-aware result.

issues.descricao: Claims checkIfIsAvailable interprets date overrides in organizerTimeZone instead of each override owner's timezone.
The new different-timezone date-override test expects the same UTC slots as the existing case and would still pass if the offset fix in slots.ts were reverted.
Claims the selected-slots availability call site passes only the user's timezone, so dateOverrides and workingHours fall back to [] and slots are checked only against busy times.
Claims getSlots uses the optional override.timeZone, so an override without it passes undefined to dayjs.tz and computes a wrong offset using the server timezone.

sugestoes.texto: getCalendarCredentials now returns calendar as a Promise<Calendar | null> because getCalendar became async and is not awaited here. Any consumer of getCalendarCredentials other than getConnectedCalendars that uses .calendar directly will get a Promise. Await getCalendar here, or make the function async, so the returned shape stays the same.

issues.descricao: Suggests wrapping the awaited dynamic app import in try-catch to handle import failures, without identifying a defect.
Claims consumers of getCalendarCredentials call methods on or null-check an un-awaited Promise; every consumer goes through getConnectedCalendars, which awaits it.
Claims the import() calls in the appStore object load every app eagerly and should be thunks; the asynchronous loading works as intended.
The commented example entry in app-store/index.ts points to ./example instead of ./_example.
Claims getVideoAdapters performs N sequential module-load round trips per request; the imports already started in parallel at module load.

sugestoes.texto: When `immediateDelete` is true, the SendGrid batch is cancelled and the function returns without deleting the WorkflowReminder row. The row is also not marked `cancelled`, so the cron cleanup never picks it up. Reminders cancelled this way (reschedule, deleted workflow, deleted step) stay in the DB as scheduled=true, unlike the SMS path and the non-immediate email path. Delete the DB row after the immediate cancel.

With immediateDelete=true the function cancels the SendGrid batch and returns without deleting the WorkflowReminder row. Before this PR every caller removed the row after cancelling, so rescheduled, deleted-workflow and deleted-step reminders are now orphaned in the DB. The callers were not changed to delete the row themselves, so the function should delete it after the cancel request succeeds.

The `immediateDelete` branch cancels the Sendgrid batch and returns without deleting or marking the WorkflowReminder row. The reschedule path in handleNewBooking uses this branch, so the old booking keeps a stale row with `scheduled=true`. Nothing removes or marks that row afterwards. Delete the row after a successful cancel.

issues.descricao: The booking-page reschedule path cancels email reminders with immediateDelete=true, which leaves the WorkflowReminder row in the DB, while the dashboard reschedule path marks it cancelled for cleanup, so the two flows are inconsistent.
Claims the code comment overstates the cancel window because the query lacks a lower bound on scheduledDate.
Claims the cron's cancel loop uses an undefined `client` variable, causing a ReferenceError.
Claims the unscheduled-reminders query re-schedules reminders marked cancelled because it lacks a cancelled filter.
Claims a hard-coded "Verification code" placeholder bypasses i18n.

sugestoes.texto: The user query's selectedCalendars select now includes the internal Google webhook identifier `googleChannelId`, which no UI code in this PR uses. If this query's result is returned to the client (for example by the `me` handler), the identifier is exposed in the response. Drop `googleChannelId` from this shared select, or strip it before the result leaves the server.

issues.descricao: Claims the cache refresh writes SelectedCalendar.updatedAt while the UI reads CalendarCache.updatedAt, so the displayed 'last updated' is never what the refresh sets.
The Delete cached data action is offered for delegation credentials that the component otherwise treats as non-modifiable, because hasCache does not check delegationCredentialId.

sugestoes.texto: The shared `unsubscribe_link` string now requires `%{unsubscribe_url}`, but only the notification mailer in user_notifications.rb passes `unsubscribe_url`. Any other email built with `add_unsubscribe_link: true` and no `unsubscribe_url` (e.g. the digest) will raise I18n::MissingInterpolationArgument when the body is built. Put the topic-specific sentence in a separate string that is added only when `unsubscribe_url` is present, or give the other callers a URL.

The `unsubscribe_link` translation now requires %{unsubscribe_url}, but `template_args` has no default for it. Any email built with add_unsubscribe_link: true and no unsubscribe_url option raises I18n::MissingInterpolationArgument from `body` and `html_part`. Provide a default (or make the string conditional) so existing callers keep working.

issues.descricao: Claims other mailers using add_unsubscribe_link do not pass unsubscribe_url, so rendering unsubscribe_link raises I18n::MissingInterpolationArgument.
Claims the unsubscribe page renders the topic title unescaped through triple braces, allowing HTML injection.
Claims the per-topic unsubscribe URL in emails is relative and cannot be resolved by email clients.
Claims the topicUnsubscribe route cannot find its template because the template lives at topic/unsubscribe.hbs.
The per-topic unsubscribe link in notification emails is built from a relative topic URL, so it has no scheme or host and cannot be opened from mail clients.
The unsubscribe_link string now requires unsubscribe_url, so any MessageBuilder caller that sets add_unsubscribe_link without it would raise a missing-interpolation error.

sugestoes.texto: The `toHaveBeenCalledTimes(5)` assertion on `applyTemplateVariables` is brittle. The 5 appears to be one call in `runShardSplitQuery` plus four from the inner `runSplitQuery`, so the number is tied to the current call structure. It would still fail if the shard-level map were removed, because the count would drop to 4, so it is not a falsification gap. Consider asserting on the interpolated outputs, or deriving the expected count, so unrelated refactors don't break the test.

issues.descricao: Claims interpolating before partitioning substitutes $__range so range queries are wrongly split; applyTemplateVariables leaves $__range untouched.
Notes test coverage of the new interpolation; no issue.
Notes test coverage of shard interpolation; no issue.
The interpolation test hardcodes the number of applyTemplateVariables calls, making it brittle to unrelated splitting changes.
The new interpolation tests do not set request.filters, so passing ad hoc filters to applyTemplateVariables is untested.
runShardSplitQuery now uses applyTemplateVariables, which strips __auto/__range scoped vars, so queries with [$__auto] reach shard sub-requests uninterpolated and fail.

sugestoes.texto: The error "sqlExpressions is not implemented" is returned for every SQL query. This includes cases where the feature flag is on, and it misleads users about the cause. Make the message say the feature is disabled or unavailable, for example "sqlExpressions feature is not enabled".

TablesList now depends on the stub DB.RunCommands, which always returns "not implemented". So NewSQLCommand always fails for any SQL, including through UnmarshalSQLCommand, which has no feature gate. The failure surfaces as a misleading BadRequest "error reading SQL command". Make the stub's failure explicit and consistent, for example return a distinct not-implemented error from NewSQLCommand, or gate all SQL entry points the same way.

The real duck DB is replaced by a stub whose TablesList, RunCommands and QueryFramesInto all return errors. sql.TablesList (used by NewSQLCommand) and SQLCommand.Execute still expect a working engine. Every SQL expression therefore fails at parse time or returns an error result, even for callers that get past the reader gate. Either keep the real implementation behind the flag, or make the consumers handle the unavailable engine explicitly.

The PR changes no test files, but the existing SQL tests in sql_command_test.go that call NewSQLCommand would now fail against the stubbed DB, because TablesList returns "not implemented". The tests were not updated to match the stubbed behaviour. They fail rather than pass falsely, so they need updating or the stub needs a real implementation.

issues.descricao: enableSqlExpressions always returns false regardless of the sqlExpressions feature flag, so SQL expressions are rejected unconditionally.
The go-duck DB was replaced by a stub whose methods always return 'not implemented', so table parsing and SQL expression execution always fail.
Claims the rejection message says 'not implemented' though the guard is a feature-flag check.
Garbled request to update db.go to use sql.NewInMemoryDB().
Vague claim that the query interface changed and lines 96 and 100 need updating.
enableSqlExpressions returns false on every path (the flag is negated and both branches return false), so SQL expressions are rejected even when FlagSqlExpressions is enabled.
Claims TablesList now calls a stub that always errors, so existing parser tests in pkg/expr/sql/parser_test.go would break.
The TypeSQL branch in nodes.go reaches UnmarshalSQLCommand → NewSQLCommand → DuckDB parsing without the enableSqlExpressions check, leaving the SQL expression RCE/LFI path reachable.

sugestoes.texto: WHAT: A denial is cached per (user, action, name, folder) for the short TTL and is checked before any permission lookup, and nothing invalidates it. WHY: if the resource is created, or the permission is granted, within the TTL after a denial, Check keeps returning Allowed=false and skips the requery. This defeats the PR goal of letting users see newly created dashboards and folders. HOW: keep the denial TTL very short, or invalidate the user's denial entries when permissions are refreshed or written.

issues.descricao: Claims a cached denial blocks access granted within the TTL window; denials are TTL-bounded like the existing permission cache.
Claims trusting cached grants while re-checking cached denials lets stale grants keep access to revoked resources; cached grants were already served for the TTL before this PR.
Claims per-resource denial entries cause unbounded cache memory growth; entries expire after the short TTL.
Claims List now serves stale cached permissions whereas it previously always queried the DB; List was already cache-backed before the change.

Claims the new denial cache is checked before any permission source and never invalidated, so a Check that ran before a resource was created or a grant was added keeps returning Allowed:false for the whole short cache TTL.
Claims the remote authz client still wraps results in a 30s LocalCache, so in remote deployments new dashboards, folders and grants stay invisible for up to 30s.

sugestoes.texto: WHAT: `readInteger` passes the result of `readLength()` straight to `read(length)`, and `readLength()` returns -1 for indefinite-length encoding (0x80). WHY: a malformed signature makes `new byte[-1]` throw an unchecked `NegativeArraySizeException` instead of the declared `IOException`, so callers that only handle `IOException` fail unexpectedly on untrusted input. HOW: reject negative lengths in `readInteger` and `readNext`, or make `read(int)` throw `IOException` when `length < 0`.

integerToBytes silently truncates an ECDSA r or s value that is larger than the curve size, keeping only the low-order bytes. Malformed or non-canonical DER signatures are therefore accepted and verified as a different signature, which makes signatures malleable. Reject oversized values instead: strip at most one leading zero sign byte, and throw if the remaining length exceeds qLength.

issues.descricao: Claims getBouncyCastleProvider returns the JDK keystore provider instead of BouncyCastle; that is the intended fallback for the BC-free authz client.
Claims readLength's -1 for indefinite-length encoding breaks length arithmetic or array allocation; the decoder only parses locally generated DER and the sequence path already rejects it.
Claims the lenient sequence parser allows malformed or trailing DER and signature malleability in verification; the parser never sees external signatures.
Claims integerToBytes can silently truncate oversized INTEGER values; inputs come from local signing and always fit the component width.
Claims createECParams/getKeyFactory throwing UnsupportedOperationException breaks EC JWK parsing in the authz client; the client does not use that path.

ASN1Decoder.readInteger passes the -1 returned by readLength for indefinite-length encoding to read(int), which allocates new byte[-1] and throws an unchecked NegativeArraySizeException instead of an IOException on malformed DER input.
integerToBytes silently truncates r/s values longer than the curve size, so non-canonical DER signatures are accepted as different values (signature malleability).
AuthzClient.create eagerly initializes CryptoIntegration, so a shaded/repackaged client that lost its ServiceLoader file fails at construction instead of only when ECDSA is used.

sugestoes.texto: WHAT: hasPermission() passes the result of getResourceTypeResource(...) to policyStore.findByResource() without a null check. WHY: the method returns null when the 'Groups' type resource doesn't exist, which causes an NPE instead of a denied permission and a 500 on group listing and user search. HOW: return false if the type resource is null.

testManageGroupMembership ends with joinGroup and never asserts that bob became a member of topGroup. It grants both the all-users MANAGE_GROUP_MEMBERSHIP permission and the group MANAGE_MEMBERSHIP permission. The test therefore cannot tell whether the group-level check is what allows the call. Assert bob's membership afterwards, and add a case where only the user permission is granted that expects Forbidden.

searchForUser used to filter the search results with usersEvaluator::canView, and the PR removed that filter. The group restriction is now applied only when getGroupIdsWithViewPermission() is non-empty, so a caller who cannot view users and has no group grants may get an unfiltered search. Keep the per-user canView filter, or confirm that toRepresentation still applies it.
hasPermission() uses the result of getResourceTypeResource() without a null check. The reviewer did not confirm that the type resource is always created, so this finding is less certain.

issues.descricao: Claims removing the canView filter from searchForUser lets admins see users they are not allowed to view.
getGroupIdsWithViewPermission scans group resources and evaluates permissions for each on every user search or count request.
Claims deleting a group under V2 triggers the removal listener, which calls GroupPermissionsV2.setPermissionsEnabled and throws UnsupportedOperationException.
Claims testManageGroupMembership never exercises the group-level manage-membership permission.
searchForUser no longer filters results with usersEvaluator::canView, so an admin with query access but no view permission and no group grants gets an unrestricted user list.

GroupPermissionsV2.canView(group) does not fall back to canView(), and the PR dropped the canViewGlobal short-circuit, so an admin with an all-groups VIEW permission is denied (and the group filtered out of listings) for any group that has its own permission resource lacking VIEW.
Claims GroupResource management-permissions endpoints call GroupPermissionsV2 methods that throw UnsupportedOperationException, causing 500s when V2 is active.

GroupPermissionsV2.hasPermission does not restrict evaluated permissions to the evaluated resource, so when falling back to the all-groups resource a permission granted on one specific group can satisfy the check for any group.

GroupsResource.getGroups no longer hoists the global canView() check, so in FGAP V2 each listed group triggers its own resource lookup and policy evaluation even when an all-groups grant would cover them all.

sugestoes.texto: WHAT: The `rolling-updates` feature is enabled only after the early `return kc` for a null update strategy, so null-strategy runs deploy without the feature. WHY: Those runs (testImageChange-null, testCacheMaxCount-null) expect a rolling-upgrade status, but the update-compatibility commands exit with FEATURE_DISABLED (4) when the feature is off, so the test may fail or not exercise the intended path. HOW: Enable the feature before the null-strategy early return and set the update spec only when a strategy is given.

issues.descricao: Claims the rolling-updates feature is not enabled for the null update strategy in UpgradeTest, so that case tests the operator without the gated feature.
Claims RECREATE_UPGRADE_EXIT_CODE changed from 4 to 3 and 4 now means feature disabled, a breaking change that needs release notes.
Claims calling picocli.exit() for the disabled-feature exit code is incorrect because it calls System.exit directly.

sugestoes.texto: WHAT: `credentialModelOpt.get()` is called without checking whether the Optional returned by `RecoveryAuthnCodesUtils.getCredential` is present, and the model built from it may have no next code. WHY: a user whose recovery-code credential is not found, or is not usable (for example a federated model with no usable code data), triggers an unhandled NoSuchElementException while rendering the login form, so the user sees a server error instead of a login challenge. HOW: check `isPresent()` and handle the empty case (for example fail the challenge or fall back) before building the model.

WHAT: `createRecoveryCodesCredential` serializes the raw, unhashed recovery codes to JSON and passes them to `updateCredential`, so the user-storage provider receives them in plaintext. WHY: the local-DB path stores the codes through `RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialModel.createFromValues` instead of persisting the raw JSON, so the user-storage path is the only one that exposes raw codes. A provider that persists them as-is keeps working recovery codes in readable form. HOW: document that user storages must hash the codes, or pass the hashed values and let validation hash the input before comparing.

The raw recovery codes are serialized to plaintext JSON and handed to the user-storage provider via updateCredential. The local-storage path hashes each code before persisting, so the federated path stores the codes unhashed in an external system. Anyone with read access to that store, or any log or dump of it, can use the codes to bypass authentication. Pass hashed codes (the same form as credentialModel's secret data) to the federated provider, or document that the provider must hash them.

issues.descricao: Claims the recovery-code validator uses non-constant-time String.equals, leaking timing information about stored codes.
Claims raw recovery codes are serialized and persisted in cleartext in user storage instead of hashed.
Claims Optional.get() on RecoveryAuthnCodesUtils.getCredential(user) without isPresent() can throw NoSuchElementException.
Plaintext recovery codes are serialized and sent to user storage providers via updateCredential, while the local path stores only hashed codes.
Recovery codes are sent to user storage providers in plaintext instead of hashed, so a provider may persist working second-factor codes.
The test user storage accepts any of the user's recovery codes rather than the specific requested code number, unlike the local provider.
BackwardsCompatibilityUserStorage.getCredentials dereferences getMyUser(user) without a null check, so it throws NullPointerException for a user missing from the provider's map.

sugestoes.texto: The truthiness check `if client_sample_rate:` treats a present but falsy value (0 or 0.0) as missing, so `sample_rate` is silently not set. Use an explicit `is not None` check instead.

The inline comments say each bucket has 1 event, but the assertions expect count == 10. The 10 is the upsampled value (1 event at client_sample_rate 0.1), so the comments contradict the assertions. Update them to say that one stored event is upsampled to 10.

issues.descricao: The test factory helper uses a truthiness check on client_sample_rate, so a rate of 0.0 is not copied to sample_rate (claimed to silently drop a legitimate value).
Claims cache keys for upsampling eligibility are built with Python's hash() and cannot be invalidated across workers; no such cache exists.
Claims changing the topEvents validation message breaks consumers asserting the old 'If topEvents needs to be at least 1' text; none exist.

sugestoes.texto: WHAT: `val["end_timestamp_precise"]` is read with a hard subscript, so a span missing the field raises KeyError. WHY: the exception propagates out of process_batch, which fails the whole batch and blocks offset commits. The consumer then crash-loops on the poison message. The `cast(SpanEvent, ...)` call does no runtime validation. HOW: use `.get()` with a fallback, or skip and count spans that lack the field.

The module docstring and key glossary still describe `span-buf:s:*` as plain sets and say the payload is simply added to the set. After this change the keys are sorted sets scored by `end_timestamp_precise`, and `add-buffer.lua` trims each one to 1000 spans, popping the lowest scores. Update the docstring to say sorted sets, the score, and the 1000-span cap.

`val["end_timestamp_precise"]` is a hard key lookup, and the `cast` to SpanEvent does no runtime validation. A span message without the field raises KeyError in process_batch, and the consumer crashes and replays that poison message. Read it defensively, for example by falling back to the message timestamp or skipping the span.

issues.descricao: Claims the redirect-resolution limit was silently cut from 10000 to 1000, so segment trees deeper than 1000 are no longer joined, and the comment still mentions 10k.
Claims a non-root span whose key equals the resolved set key unions the key with itself and then unlinks it, deleting the buffered segment.
Claims a span message missing end_timestamp_precise raises KeyError and aborts the whole batch.
Claims OptimizedCursorPaginator's negative-offset branch passes cursor.offset directly into queryset slicing when advanced features are enabled.
Claims BasePaginator.get_result sets start_offset to an unclamped offset for previous-page cursors, allowing negative slicing.
Claims OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_item_key applies floor/ceil to a datetime key, raising TypeError.
Claims accessing organization_context.member.has_global_access raises AttributeError when organization_context is None.
process_batch indexes end_timestamp_precise directly, so a span without the field raises KeyError and fails the whole consumer batch.
Claims span_count counts pre-existing spans in set_key, so zpopmin evicts far more than the overflow above 1000 and discards valid spans.
